map.一战德军密码，6x6 方阵（A-Z + 0-9）+ 列置换。: A German WWI field cipher built on a 6×6 square (A–Z plus 0–9) and column transposition.
map.一战德军使用的双层密码：先用 6×6 方阵做代换，再按密钥做列置换。: A two-layer cipher used by the German army in WWI: a 6×6 square performs the substitution first, then a keyword drives the column transposition.

map.：代换结果按行写入宽度为密钥长度的表格，按密钥字母序重排列，再按列读出密文。: : the substituted output is written row by row into a table as wide as the keyword, the columns are reordered in the alphabetical order of the keyword letters, and the ciphertext is then read off column by column.
map.：属古典密码，可用重合指数配合列置换分析破译，仅作教学用途。: : it is a classical cipher, breakable with the index of coincidence combined with transposition analysis — for teaching purposes only.

map.手工演算列置换：先用 6×6 方阵把明文转成 ADFGVX 字母对，再按密钥给列: Work the column transposition by hand: first turn the plaintext into ADFGVX letter pairs with the 6×6 square, then number and reorder the columns by keyword — and see for yourself why the two-layer structure of substitution plus transposition is far stronger than a plain substitution.
map.先按 6×6 方阵把字符替换为 ADFGVX 两字母，再按密钥列置换；如 P →: Each character is first replaced by two ADFGVX letters from the 6×6 square, then the columns are transposed by the keyword; P sits at row A, column D, so it becomes `AD`.
map.这些字母在莫尔斯电码中区分度大，减少传输误码。: Because they are easy to tell apart in Morse code, which cut down transmission errors.
map.为什么 ADFGVX 比普通替换密码难破？: Why is ADFGVX harder to break than an ordinary substitution cipher?
map.它先做分数化代换（一个字母 → 两个符号），再做列置换，破坏了单字母与单符号的对: It performs fractionating substitution first (one letter becomes two symbols) and then column transposition, which destroys the one-to-one link between a letter and a symbol and so defeats frequency analysis. Breaking it means recovering both the square and the transposition key — the French cryptanalyst Georges Painvin managed it in 1918 only by studying repeating patterns.
